facts.claim: A Learner Licence must be obtained before a new Driving Licence can be granted in Gujarat.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: An applicant is required to obtain a learning license in order to get new driving license.

facts.claim: Nationally, a non-diplomat applicant must apply for a Learner's Licence before proceeding to a Driving Licence.
facts.subject: driving_licence

detail.exception: Diplomats may apply for a Driving Licence directly

facts.evidence:
1. If you are a Diplomat: You can apply for Driving License directly.

2. If you are a Non-Diplomat: You have to apply for Learner's License, before proceeding for Driving License.

facts.claim: The permanent Driving Licence application is made in Form 4 together with the Learner's Licence held for that class of vehicle.
facts.subject: driving_licence

detail.mustAccompany: Learner's Licence for the same class of vehicle

facts.evidence: An application in Form 4, for a permanent driving licence shall be made along with the Learners' Licence obtained for such class of vehicle.

facts.claim: An applicant must have held a valid Learner's Licence for at least 30 days before being competent to appear for the driving test of competence.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: The applicant who has held a valid Learners' Licence, for a period of at least 30 days, shall be competent to appear for the test of competence.

facts.claim: Learner's Licence validity is 6 months and a New Driving Licence can be applied for after 30 days.
facts.subject: learner_licence
facts.evidence: Learner's Licence validity is for 6 months, and you can apply for New Driving Licence after 30 days.

facts.claim: The Learner Licence is valid throughout India for 6 months, and on expiry the whole process must be repeated afresh.
facts.subject: learner_licence
facts.evidence: The Learner Licence is valid through out India for a period of 6 months only. In case of expiry of the Learner Licence the applicant needs to repeat the process afresh.

facts.claim: An expired Learner's Licence cannot be renewed; only a new Learner's Licence can be obtained.
facts.subject: learner_licence
facts.evidence:
Learner's License validity is for 6 Months and post expiry you can only get a new Learner's License.

The expired License cannot be renewed.

facts.claim: The Driving Licence must be applied for before the Learner Licence expires and the driving test completed within that window.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: No. Apply for Driving licence before your Learner Licence expires and complete the driving test.

facts.claim: In Gujarat the driving test may be taken after a gap of 30 days from obtaining the learning licence.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: One can appear for driving test after a gap of 30 days of obtaining learning license.

facts.claim: In Gujarat the learning licence is valid for 6 months and the driving test must be taken within that validity period.
facts.subject: learner_licence
facts.evidence: Learning license is valid for a period of 6 months only, therefore, an applicant is required to appear for driving test within the validity period.

facts.claim: A re-test can be applied for after 7 days.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: Re-test can be applied after 7 days.

facts.claim: After failing the driving skill test three times, the retest fee may only be deposited 60 days after the last failed attempt.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: Yes, you are able to deposit the fee but after the 60 days of last failure attempt.

facts.claim: In Gujarat a person failing the learner licence knowledge test may re-take it after a gap of 24 hours.
facts.subject: learner_licence
facts.evidence: A person failing in the test can appear for the re-test after a gap of 24 hours.

facts.claim: An applicant under 18 may be granted a learner's licence for a motor cycle without gear only with the written consent of the person having care of the applicant.
facts.subject: learner_licence
facts.evidence: An applicant under the age of eighteen years shall be granted a learner's license to drive a motor cycle without gear except with the consent in writing of the person having the care of the person desiring a learner's license.

facts.claim: An applicant who has completed 18 years is eligible to apply for a driving licence for a motor vehicle other than a transport vehicle.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: The applicant who has completed the age of eighteen years of age is eligible to apply for a driving licence to drive a motor vehicle other than a transport vehicle.

facts.claim: An applicant who has completed 20 years is eligible to apply for a licence to drive a transport vehicle.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: An applicant who has completed twenty years of age will be eligible for applying for a licence to drive a transport vehicle.

facts.claim: The national age criteria are 16 for MCWOG, 18 for LMV and MCWG, 20 for Transport Vehicle and 18 for Conductor Licence.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence:
The age criteria are as follows:

1. 16 years of age for MCWOG vehicle class (Private Vehicle)

2. 18 years of age for LMV (Light Motor Vehicle) & MCWG vehicle class (Private Vehicle)

3. 20 years of age for Transport Vehicle

4. 18 years of age for Conductor License

facts.claim: In Gujarat a person must have completed 16 years to obtain a licence for two wheelers without gear.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: A person should have completed 16 years to obtain license for 2 wheelers without gear.

facts.claim: In Gujarat a person must have completed 18 years for two wheelers with gear, motor-car, tractor and other non-transport vehicles.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: A person should have completed 18 years age to obtain license for 2 wheelers with gear, Motor-car, Tractor and other non-transport vehicles.

facts.claim: In Gujarat a transport vehicle licence requires age 20, a pass in standard 8, and one year of light motor vehicle driving experience.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: For transport vehicles, a person should have completed 20 years of age. In addition he should be passed standard 8th pass and should have experience of 1 year driving a light motor vehicle.

facts.claim: MCWOG means Motor cycle without Gear, MCWG means Motor Cycle with Gear, and MC50CC means motor vehicle with engine capacity less than 50CC.
facts.subject: driving_licence

detail.MC50CC: Motor vehicle with engine capacity less than 50CC

facts.evidence:
Full Form for MCWOG: Motor cycle without Gear.

MCWG: Motor Cycle with Gear

MC50CC: Motor vehicle with engine capacity less than 50CC

facts.claim: A colour blind applicant may apply for a driving or learner's licence but must obtain a medical certificate from a hospital.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: Yes, you need to get the medical certificate from the hospital.

facts.claim: A one-eyed applicant cannot apply for a driving or learner's licence.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence:
[Can one eyed applicant apply for the driving/learner's license](https://parivahan.gov.in/en/node/111)

No

facts.claim: An illiterate applicant may apply for a Driving Licence in India.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence:
[I am illiterate, can I apply for the driving License/Learner's License](https://parivahan.gov.in/en/node/114)

Yes, you can apply for Driving License in India.

facts.claim: The official CMVR Form 2 annexure lists ten alternative documents accepted as Proof of Address and Age, and only one need be selected if the same proof covers both.
facts.subject: learner_licence

detail.note: Select only one if the proof is common for Address and Age
acceptedDocuments: Pay slip issued by any office of the State Government or Central Government or a local Body
Affidavit sworn before an Executive Magistrate or Notary Public or First Class Judicial Magistrate
A certificate granted by a Registered Medical Practitioner not below the rank of Civil Surgeon as to the age of the applicant
Any other document or documents as may be specified by State Government

facts.claim: CMVR Form 2 lists eight further documents to be enclosed or uploaded if applicable, including Form 1, Form 1A, Form 5 and a parent/guardian declaration for minors.
facts.subject: learner_licence

documents: Self Declaration for Physical Fitness in Form-1
Medical Certificate in Form-1A (to be provided if the applicant is applying for renewal and is above 40 years of age or applying for Transport Licence)
Driving Certificate issued by Driving School or Establishments in Form 5
Parent or Guardian Declaration in case of applicant who is a minor
Valid proof of passport and visa (for International Driving Permit only)
Proof of legal presence in India in addition to proof of residence in case of Foreigners

facts.evidence:
Other documents to be enclosed or uploaded if applicable
1. Self Declaration for Physical Fitness in Form-1
2. Medical Certificate in Form-1A (to be provided if the applicant is applying for renewal and is above 40 years of age or applying for Transport Licence)
3. Driving Certificate issued by Driving School or Establishments in Form 5
4. Parent or Guardian Declaration in case of applicant who is a minor
5. Photograph
6. Valid proof of passport and visa (for International Driving Permit only)
7. Proof of legal presence in India in addition to proof of residence in case of Foreigners
8. Other documents, if any

facts.claim: Gujarat's Commissionerate of Transport lists seven alternative documents accepted as proof of age.
facts.subject: learner_licence
facts.evidence: School Leaving Certificate, Birth Certificate, Passport, Pan Card, L.I.C. Policy or a Certificate from Civil Surgeon or a Doctor equivalent to that can be submitted as a proof of age.

facts.claim: Gujarat's Commissionerate of Transport lists nine alternative documents accepted as proof of address.
facts.subject: learner_licence

acceptedDocuments: receipt of House Tax with address
Pay Slip of Central/State/Local self Government
an Affidavit from the applicant to that effect

facts.evidence: School Leaving Certificate, Passport, L.I.C. Policy, Electoral Voter I-Card, Light Bill, Telephone Bill, receipt of House Tax with address, Pay Slip of Central/State/Local self Government or an Affidavit from the applicant to that effect can be submitted asthe proof for address.

facts.claim: Address proof must be enclosed with the Form 2 application in the case of a New Learner's Licence or New Driving Licence.
facts.subject: learner_licence
facts.evidence: Address (proof to be enclosed, in case of New Learner's Licence or New Driving Present Address (shall be printed on Licence)

facts.claim: Form 1 (self-declaration as to physical fitness) is mandatory for the Learner Licence test.
facts.subject: learner_licence
facts.evidence:
[Is Form 1 Mandatory for Learner Licence Test?](https://parivahan.gov.in/en/node/161)

Yes, Form 1 is self declaration medical

facts.claim: Form 1A (medical certificate) is not mandatory for the Learner Licence test; it is required only for applicants aged 40 years or above.
facts.subject: learner_licence
facts.evidence:
[Is Form 1A Mandatory for Learner Licence Test?](https://parivahan.gov.in/en/node/160)

No,

Medical Certificate (FORM 1A) is required for applicants having age equal to or above 40 years.

facts.claim: For a New Driving Licence, Form 1A is required for applicants aged 40 or above; applicants under 40 submit Form 1.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: Medical Certificate (FORM 1A) is required for applicants having age equal to or above 40 years, in case of less than 40 you need to submit FORM 1.

facts.subject: learner_licence

detail.downloadPath: https://parivahan.gov.in/parivahan >> Informational Services >> DownloadableForms > AllForms >> Form-1 and Form-1A

facts.evidence:
Yes. Form 1 should be invariably attached with Form 1A ( Medical Fitness)

facts.claim: In Gujarat the application for both learning and driving licence is made in Form No.2/4 with Medical Certificate in Form No.1(A) attached.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence: An applicant is required to apply in Form No.2/4 for the purpose of both learning as well as driving license, Medical Certificate in Form No.1 (A) is also required to be attached.

facts.claim: Form 2 is the single form of application for a Learner's Licence, a Driving Licence, addition of a class of vehicle, renewal, or change of address or name.

facts.evidence: FORM 2 *[Refer Rules 10, 14, 17 and 18]* FORM OF APPLICATION FOR LEARNER'S LICENCE OR DRIVING LICENCE OR ADDITION OF A NEW CLASS OF VEHICLE OR RENEWAL OF DRIVING LICENCE OR CHANGE OF ADDRESS OR NAME

facts.claim: A passport size photograph is required with Form 2 and for online applications must not exceed 50 KB.
facts.subject: learner_licence
facts.evidence: Space for passport size photograph (Upload the photo for online application of the size not more than 50 KB)

facts.claim: A minor applicant's Form 2 must carry a parent/guardian declaration under sub-section (2) of section 7 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 consenting to the learner's licence.
facts.subject: learner_licence

detail.statute: sub-section (2) of section 7 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988

facts.claim: Uploaded documents must be a single JPEG or PDF file within the given size limit.
facts.subject: learner_licence
facts.evidence: Document need to be single jpeg copy or PDF file in the given size only. You may use online option to compress them.

facts.claim: Learner Licence applications are made online on the Sarathi service portal via the 'New Learning Licence' link, and where online transactions are not enabled the CMV Form-2 may be submitted to the jurisdictional licensing authority.
facts.subject: learner_licence

detail.offlineFallback: prescribed CMV Form-2 / Unified Form to the jurisdictional licensing authority

facts.evidence: Applicants can visit [https://sarathi.parivahan.gov.in/sarathiservice](https://sarathi.parivahan.gov.in/sarathiservice) and apply for Learner Licence ONLINE by following the link "New Learning Licence " Applicants should take print of the duly filled-in ONLINE application along with the reference number and submit at the chosen RTO office. Wherever the ONLINE transactions are not enabled, the applicants can submit the application in the prescribed CMV Form-2 / Unified Form to the jurisdictional licensing authority.

facts.claim: The Learner Licence application flow on Sarathi is: select state, choose 'Application for New Learners License' from the Learner's License menu, fill the form, then visit the RTO on the scheduled date with original documents and fee slip.
facts.subject: learner_licence

detail.menuPath: Learner's License > Application for New Learners License

facts.evidence:
Steps to for Learners' Licence for New Learner's License (Flow may be differ from state to state):-

1. Visit https://sarathi.parivahan.gov.in/

2. Select concerned state

3. Click on "Application for New Learners License" from "Learner's License" menu

4. Fill up Learner's License application Form

5. Click on Next Button to proceed

6. Visit RTO on scheduled date with original documents & Fee Slip

facts.claim: The permanent Driving Licence application flow on Sarathi is: select state, choose 'New Driving Licence' from the Driving Licence menu, enter the Learning Licence Number and Date of Birth, fill the form, then visit the RTO on the scheduled date.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence:
Steps to follow for New Driving License :-

1. Visit https://sarathi.parivahan.gov.in/

2. Select concerned state

3. Click on "New Driving Licence" from "Driving Licence" menu

4. Enter your "Learning License Number" & "Date of Birth" to proceed further

5. Fill up application Form

6.Click on Next Button to proceed

7. Visit RTO on scheduled date with original documents & Fee Slip

facts.evidence: Schedule an appointment for the test of competence online by visiting the website or any RTO office where such facility exists. In other cases schedule an appointment directly at the Office Concerned.

facts.claim: The Learner Licence test is an online test but must be taken at the concerned RTO or its authorised learning licence test centre, not from home.
facts.subject: learner_licence

detail.location: concerned RTO or their authorized learning license test center

facts.evidence:
[Can I give exam from home or I will have to go to the concerned RTO?](https://parivahan.gov.in/en/node/90)

You need to report the concerned RTO or their authorized learning license test center.

facts.claim: The Learner Licence is obtained by passing the online STALL test, after which one month must elapse before appearing for the driving test.
facts.subject: learner_licence
facts.evidence:
Yes, you have to pass the online test (STALL Test) to get Learner's License. After the completion of its one

month you need to appear for driving test to get your driving license.

facts.claim: To obtain a driving licence one must undergo a Motor Driving test on a vehicle, conducted at the RTO.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence:
[What type of test would be conducted at RTO?](https://parivahan.gov.in/en/node/184)

To obtaining a driving license one needs to undergo a Motor Driving test (on vehicle)

facts.claim: The applicant should bring a vehicle of the type to which the driving licence application relates and must satisfy the testing officer per Rule 15(2) of the CMVR.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence:
The applicant should bring a vehicle of the type to which the application relates.
- The applicant should satisfy the officer conducting the test regarding his capability to drive the vehicle and his ability to perform the tasks specified in Rule-15(2) of the CMVR.

facts.claim: In Gujarat the learner licence knowledge test is on computer, asks 15 random questions of which 11 must be answered correctly, with 48 seconds allowed per question.
facts.subject: learner_licence

detail.topics: Rules and Regulations of traffic, and traffic signage

facts.evidence:
To obtain Learning License, Knowledge Test through computer is required to be passed.
Subject like Rules and Regulations of traffic, and traffic signage's are included the test.
15 questions are asked in the test at random, out of which 11 questions are required to be answered correctly to pass the test.
48 seconds are allowed to answer each question.

facts.claim: In Gujarat a driving test is compulsory for a permanent driving licence and is conducted on the same kind of vehicle applied for.
facts.subject: driving_licence

detail.vehicle: same kind of vehicle for which application is made

facts.evidence:
Driving test is compulsory to obtain permanent driving license|
One can appear for driving test after a gap of 30 days of obtaining learning license.
Driving test is conducted on same kind of vehicle for which application is made for obtaining driving license has been made.

facts.claim: A certificate from a Driving Training School exempts the applicant from the Learner's Licence test, subject to state jurisdiction.

facts.evidence:

facts.claim: In Gujarat the learning licence is handed to the applicant in person on the day of the knowledge test, while the driving licence is sent by speed post to the address given in the application.

detail.dlDelivery: speed post to the address in the application

facts.evidence:
Learning license is delivered to the applicant in person on the same day when he comes for knowledge test.|
Driving license is sent by speed post at the address mentioned by the applicant in his application.

facts.claim: Nationally, a candidate who passes the test of competence is issued a driving licence sent through speed post to the address furnished.

detail.delivery: speed post to the address furnished

facts.evidence: The candidate who passes the test of competence successfully will be issued with a driving licence and sent through speed post to the address furnished.

facts.claim: A driving licence is required to drive a motor vehicle in any public place.
facts.subject: driving_licence

detail.legalBasis: effective driving licence issued by the Licensing Authority

facts.evidence: No person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place unless he holds an effective driving licence issued to him by the Licensing Authority, authorising him to drive the vehicle.

facts.claim: A private driving licence is valid for 20 years from date of issue or until the holder attains 40 years of age, whichever comes earlier.
facts.subject: driving_licence
facts.evidence:
Private Driving license is valid for 20 years from the date of issue or till the holder attains 40 years of age, which comes earlier.

After the age of 40 the Driving licence will be issued for 10 years & then 5 years subsequently.

notFound: Exact deep-link Sarathi URLs for 'Application for New Learners License' and 'New Driving Licence' pre-filtered to Gujarat. Sarathi gates these behind a POST state-selection step and the site map returned only stateSelection.do ('Home') and applViewStatus.do ('Application Status'). Only the portal entry point plus the officially documented menu path could be verified.

A single official reconciliation of the Form 1A medical-certificate trigger. Three official sources disagree: parivahan.gov.in FAQ says age 40+, CMVR Form 2 annexure says 'applying for renewal and is above 40 years of age or applying for Transport Licence', the Sarathi LL FAQ says Form 1A is required with Form 1 unconditionally, and the Gujarat COT page says age 50+ for renewal.

Register Your Grievance / Track Your Grievance URLs on cot.gujarat.gov.in. The menu labels are printed on the page but the hrefs are JavaScript-generated and absent from the served HTML, so no URL could be quoted.

A current, official Gujarat-specific fee schedule for LL and DL. The Gujarat COT page quotes Rs.25 test fee + Rs.30 per category (LL) and Rs.200 smart card + Rs.50 per category (DL), which conflicts with the central Parivahan schedule (Rs.150 / Rs.50 / Rs.300 / Rs.200). No official page reconciling the two was found.

Official Apple App Store listing and bundle identifier for mParivahan / NextGen mParivahan. Only the Android package (com.nic.mparivahan) is officially verifiable; DigiLocker's iOS id (1320618078) was verifiable but mParivahan's was not.

Public counter working hours and days for RTO Ahmedabad, RTO Surat and RTO Vadodara. The official cot.gujarat.gov.in RTO/ARTO directory publishes only code, address, STD code, phone, fax, email and a map link.

National-level specification of the LL test format (number of questions, pass mark, time per question). Only the Gujarat COT page states 15 questions / 11 correct / 48 seconds; no parivahan.gov.in page confirms these numbers.

Whether Aadhaar is mandatory for LL/DL in Gujarat. CMVR Form 2 records Aadhaar only 'if already available with the applicant' and lists it as one of ten alternative age/address proofs; no official page states it is compulsory.
The two cached files .firecrawl/pv-ll.md and .firecrawl/pv-dl.md contain 'Page not found' rather than content; no facts were drawn from them.

Direct Firecrawl access to cot.gujarat.gov.in was blocked (ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED across 6+ retries). Those three Gujarat pages were fetched over plain HTTPS instead and cached as raw HTML; evidence quotes are from a tag-stripped rendering of that HTML rather than a Firecrawl markdown extraction.
